recovery_estimator: two_pool (recovery.json regenerated 2026-09-26 with --estimator two_pool --holdout --n-shuffles 200). Each pure pool is split into a reference half and a DISJOINT draw half (--holdout), so no particle mixed into the sweep is also an estimator reference -- this removes a train-on-test leak (mixtures were previously drawn from the same full pools used as references); measured immaterial (held-out slopes match the leaky ones to ~0.02 for the clean pairs, hb noisier at small n). The purity sweep reads each mixed pool's fraction with the 2-pool reference-mixture MLE on both pure pools' KDE densities -- the estimator the data selected: 0-pool is compressed toward 0.5 by overdispersion (slopes 0.60-0.94), and the two 1-pool variants (one pure pool's within-variance, ref-A or ref-B) diverge robustly on hk-atpase (gap 0.37 +/- 0.03 over held-out splits, the tell its two states' within-scales differ); hb also shows a gap on average but it is too unstable to trust (0.22 +/- 0.14, small n=2539) -- an earlier leaky reading (0.31) overstated it. CAVEAT: on a purity sweep 2-pool is partly self-referential -- it recovers A/B mixtures from the A/B densities the sweep was built from -- so slope~=1 attests ESTIMATOR CONSISTENCY, not per-pair discriminability magnitude; read d2/coherence for magnitude and the 0->1A->1B->2 ladder for when 2 pools are required. SHUFFLE NULL: recovery.json carries a 200-permutation label-shuffle null (shuffle_null block); observed slopes sit 5-9 sigma above it (null centered ~0, sd 0.12-0.21) for every pair, so the recovered separation is real, not chance. A label shuffle CANNOT separate structural from batch/session difference (the two pools are separate accessions); the batch control is twin_floor (a same-state re-score through the pipeline), which has NOT been run.

amplitude_scale_limitation: KNOWN LIMITATION (diagnosed 2026-09-26, not acted on). Across all systems 2*mean(Lambda) reads ~0.47-0.55x the closed-form known_pose_d2 (implied_amplitude_scale ~0.5, fractional_error_mean ~-0.5), uniform across 2.12 and 4.0 A/px. Diagnosis: NOT a formula bug (known_pose_d2 and known_pose_log_ratio share one code path, so E[Lambda]=d2/2 by construction) and NOT power asymmetry (amplitude_ratio ~1, so use_power_asymmetry's lever ~0). It is a MISSING HIGH-FREQUENCY ENVELOPE in the forward model: templates are half-maps (near full-resolution density) but particle images are attenuated at high k by radiation damage, motion and detector MTF. Evidence: --amplitude-shells 12 on ste2 and msba both fit an a(k) that ROLLS OFF within the band (ste2 0.52->0.23, msba 0.90->0.55; driver: 'templates carry MORE high-frequency power than the data'). Fitting a(k) recovers the implied scale partway (ste2 0.53->0.69, msba 0.47->0.57) but not to 1, and leaves a separate large decoherence (ste2 0.52, msba 0.39) untouched. IMPLICATION: absolute d2/coherence MAGNITUDES are understated by this envelope and must not be quoted as absolute discriminability without the a(k) caveat; composition recovery (purity slope/f_a) is scale-tolerant under two_pool and is unaffected. The operating point still fits a SCALAR contrast (no envelope); fitting a(k) or an explicit B-factor as default would correct it but needs a re-score and has not been done. Diagnostics are scratch on ribo (campaign/score/ste2/score_a_ashells.json, campaign/score/msba_ashells.json); committed pools/scores were NOT changed.

files_per_system: pool_<state>.npy (per-particle log-ratio Lambda), pool_<state>_d2.npy (per-particle closed-form known_pose_d2, aligned 1:1 with the Lambda -- verified 2*mean(Lambda)/mean(d2) reproduces each score's implied_amplitude_scale; absent for hb, which was not re-scored under score_pool), score_<state>.json (self-documenting: commit, full arguments, result), recovery.json (purity recovery under the two_pool estimator -- see recovery_estimator; the estimator is recorded inside recovery.json's result and arguments); msba/fanac use state-name files, hb uses pool_r/pool_t, the campaign systems use pool_a/pool_b + score_a/score_b (a=state_a, b=state_b, mapping documented per system)
campaign_note: The five Tier-1 campaign systems (nkcc1, slc19a3, slco2a1, ste2, hk-atpase) were fetched, co-refined and scored at commit 5ce4383d via deploy/orc/_process_campaign.sh (registry docs/planning/process_registry.json) and scored with campaign/score_campaign.py. State labels are the deposited PDB IDs (the grid is the state label). d2_pool_split.mean is mean(Lambda_a)-mean(Lambda_b); .median the same for medians. For discriminability MAGNITUDE read d2/coherence, not the raw d2_pool_split gap; the two_pool recovery (purity_fa/slope) is an estimator-consistency check, not a magnitude (see recovery_estimator).

hk-atpase.note: WEAK / low-contrast pair. map_b resampled 4.001 -> 4.011 A/px. Template baseline coherence ~0.49 at both poles (clean systems 0.83-0.93); the 7w4a/8ijl states share 69% of atoms and were admitted via min_shared_fraction 0.5. Under held-out two_pool composition recovers (purity_fa 1.002, slope 1.008, and 9 sigma above the label-shuffle null), but that is EXPECTED given both references (see recovery_estimator caveat) and does NOT lift the weak-pair status: the two 1-pool estimates DISAGREE sharply and stably (ref-A slope 1.18 vs ref-B 0.81, gap 0.37 +/- 0.03 over held-out splits, against ~0.95-1.01 agreement on the clean pairs), the tell that the two states' within-scales differ and one pool cannot de-bias both. The old pool-free readout was purity_fa 0.635, slope 0.62. d2_pool_split (mean 48, median 27) is inflated by large pool variance and OVERSTATES discriminability -- read baseline coherence and the 1-pool spread, not the raw gap or the 2-pool slope. Do not present alongside the clean pairs without this caveat.

hb.note: RE-SCORED first-class 2026-09-26 (box 128 @ 2.04 A/px, n=2613/4000) from refinements recovered off orc (CS-hb-rt-1 R, CS-hb-rt-2 T), superseding the old box-32 dump pools. map_b (T) was power-matched to map_a (R) first -- the two independent refinements differed 1.587x in amplitude (see provenance map_power_match). Now at the campaign operating point and clean: slope 1.023, purity_fa 1.016, 8.5 sigma above the shuffle null. Held-out 1-pool(A/B) disagree by a STABLE 0.204 +/- 0.008 (the dump's 0.22 +/- 0.14 was small-n noise), so hb has moderate real heterogeneity -- intermediate between the clean cluster (<=0.09) and hk-atpase (0.37), and needs two pools.
